subject: Security pricing walkthrough: KMS/HSM and residency options
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@healthgrid.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security pricing walkthrough: KMS/HSM and residency options

Hi Dana — thanks again for taking time today. As promised, a concise summary of the pricing options we walked through for HealthGrid's pilot and initial rollout, plus the asks we discussed so procurement can move this forward.

Key scope items (pilot):
- KMS integration for envelope key management (per-tenant key API).
- Optional HSM-backed keys for regulated EU residency workloads (per-seat HSM license + per-GB encrypted throughput).
- Audit log retention: 90 days default (longer retention available as an add-on).

High-level pricing models (rough ballpark; exacts in attached workbook):
- KMS (cloud-managed): $0.02 per 1k key ops, included in hosted plan for pilot up to X ops/day.
- HSM seat (dedicated, FIPS-backed): $6,500 seat/month for production SLA; pilot discounted model below.
- Audit logs: $0.10/GB ingested per month for first 90 days; tiered pricing beyond that.
- Data residency (EU): one-time residency activation fee + 10% residency premium on unit rates.

Concession options for pilot we propose internally:
- Discount the first 30 days of HSM seats (waive seat fee) for a 90-day pilot.
- Provide a SOC2 snapshot and evidence package to accelerate procurement (see attached).
- Fixed-price pilot invoice to simplify PO (e.g., $12,000 for 90-day pilot including up to 2 HSM seats usage, audit logs up to 1TB).

Next items for HealthGrid procurement:
1) Confirm whether the pilot needs HSM seats active in EU at launch or if KMS-only is acceptable for initial 30 days.
2) Procurement contact + PO timeline (we can issue fixed-scope invoice).
3) Any hard constraints on payment terms (Net30/Net45) or vendor paperwork.

Attachments: healthgrid_soc2_snapshot.pdf (SOC2 excerpt), kms_vs_hsm_cost_model.xlsx (detailed workbook).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the invoice layout.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security pricing walkthrough: KMS/HSM and residency options

Sean — thanks for the summary and for the call earlier. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and engineering: 

- On audit log costs: can you confirm whether logs are metered on ingest or on stored GB? We have compliance that requires 12 months of logs for certain gateways; that changes economics a lot.
- For EU residency: is HSM mandatory or can we start with KMS + geo-fenced storage while we validate controls?
- Procurement: we prefer a single fixed invoice for the pilot. Net30 is our standard unless there is a compelling reason.

Also looping in Oliver from CloudSec (copied) — they will want to review the SOC2 snapshot and confirm the HSM/key custody model.

Best,
Dana

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Security pricing walkthrough: KMS/HSM and residency options

On Thu, Aug 14, 2025 at 11:05 AM Dana Morris <dana.morris@healthgrid.com> wrote:
> - On audit log costs: can you confirm whether logs are metered on ingest or on stored GB? We have compliance that requires 12 months of logs for certain gateways; that changes economics a lot.
> - For EU residency: is HSM mandatory or can we start with KMS + geo-fenced storage while we validate controls?

Dana — quick answers from product/pricing perspective: 
- Audit logs are metered on stored GB per month. We bill based on the average stored GB in a month (ledgered). For long‑term retention (>=12 months) we recommend our cold-tier archive at $0.03/GB-month with a 30-day retrieval SLA.
- EU residency: HSM is not strictly mandatory for all EU-residency workloads. For many customers KMS with customer-managed keys + residency-guarded storage meets regulatory needs for initial pilots. HSM seats are recommended when the customer requires FIPS 140-2/3 hardware attestation for signing or when there is a contractual requirement to separate key material from cloud HSM providers.

Pilot concession proposal (we can confirm formally):
- Waive first 30 days of HSM seat fee for up to 2 seats if HealthGrid signs the fixed-scope pilot PO (see example below).
- Provide SOC2 snapshot now + complete attestations within 10 business days.
- Offer a 10% pilot discount on audit log charges if pilot goes to production within 6 months.

Suggested fixed pilot invoice (example):
- Pilot fee (90 days): $12,000 — covers platform usage, onboarding support, and up to 1TB audit log storage in active tier.
- HSM seat (discounted for pilot): $0 for first 30 days, then prorated at $3,250/month for remaining months if seats remain active.

If procurement wants Net30 we can accept that for pilot invoice; if they require Net45 we will need to route to finance for approval (possible but slower).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Security pricing walkthrough: KMS/HSM and residency options

Dana / team — following up with the concrete artifacts and next steps. Attached is the detailed cost model (kms_vs_hsm_cost_model.xlsx) that breaks down: per-op KMS pricing, HSM seat amortization, audit log tiers (active/cold), and residency surcharge math. A few clarifications inline: 

- Logs: we meter on stored GB (monthly average). For your 12-month retention case I mocked a 1TB active + 11TB cold snapshot scenario in the workbook — see tab 'Retention-12m'.
- EU residency: you can absolutely start with KMS + residency-enabled storage; HSM only becomes required if your compliance team requires hardware isolation for signing or key proof.

Actionable next steps: 
1) Dana to confirm whether HealthGrid wants HSM seats at pilot start or deferred to month 2.
2) Procurement to confirm PO amount and payment terms (we can issue an example fixed invoice for $12,000).
3) Oliver to review SOC2 snapshot and respond with any gaps by EOD Wed.

DocuSign SOW (draft): https://www.docusign.com/submit/HG-4532-sow
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/records/contacts/4532

If helpful I can run a 20-minute procurement walkthrough on Wednesday at 10am ET.

Thanks — attaching the workbook and SOC2 excerpt again.

—Sean

Sean / Monica — procurement here. We reviewed the pilot proposal and can approve a fixed pilot PO for $12,000 under the following terms:

- Scope: 90-day pilot as described (platform, onboarding support, up to 1TB active audit log).
- HSM seats: not required at launch; procurement requests Redwood hold the option to add up to 2 HSM seats with 30 days' notice and prorated billing.
- Compliance evidence: please route SOC2 snapshot and any additional attestation into our vendor portal (we'll send upload instructions).

Please send a final SOW and invoice addressed to: HealthGrid, Attn: Procurement, 450 Market St, Suite 1200, San Francisco, CA 94105.
